label: Jacques F. Vallee
narrative: Vallee is the provenance chain. Where Nolan brought the instruments, Vallee brought the samples and, crucially, the fifty-year paper trail attached to them. Trained in mathematics at Paris (1959) and astrophysics at Lille (1961), with a Northwestern PhD (1967), he joined Douglas Engelbart's Augmentation Research Center at SRI International in 1971 - the same institution and period as Puthoff's psychoenergetics work - and succeeded Paul Baran as principal investigator on the NSF computer-networking project, building PLANET, one of the first ARPANET conferencing systems. He then spent 1987-2010 as a Silicon Valley general partner. Across all of it he assembled a physical collection of alleged UAP-associated materials with documented case files: the 1957 Ubatuba magnesium fragments, the 1977 Council Bluffs molten mass, and the 1945 San Antonio, New Mexico 'Trinity' case material he wrote up with Paola Harris in 2021. He was a consultant to Robert Bigelow's National Institute for Discovery Science and a member of the Bigelow Aerospace scientific advisory board, which puts him inside the same Bigelow ecosystem that produced BAASS and the AAWSAP contract. His 2022 collaboration with Nolan is the moment the collection met modern instrumentation. The custody problem here is honest and stated: Vallee's samples come with newspaper reporting, police photographs, fire-department accounts and witness interviews - a civil chain, not a federal one - and that is exactly why the government-held material remains the missing term. His lifetime archive went to the Archives of the Impossible at Rice University, with embargoes running to 2028-2031: a dark segment with a published end date.
